findings.explanation: The answer rests on one trial, but nowhere does the script say it covered a small app over a short period. The package lists that limit. The authors also say they could see only short-term maintainability. This matters because the hook asks about changing the code 'next year'.
findings.suggestion: Scope the answer, for example 'In the one trial that tested it, on a small app over a short time, no: ...'. If the writer has no passage for the scope, set generation.needsEvidence.

findings.explanation: 'Many of the issues they introduced still survive' is the authors' wording. Their own figure is 22.7% of tracked issues, and only 7.5-14.8% of commits introduce any issue at all. A viewer hearing 'many' with no size will picture most of the code, which overstates the finding.
findings.suggestion: Say 'about a fifth of the issues they introduced still survive' (cite L857), or keep 'some of'. Citing the figure needs that passage in the corpus, so set generation.needsEvidence if it is not there.

findings.explanation: The package limit says this experiment's 69 participants were mostly students. The takeaway (s28-s29) applies the result to reviewing a colleague's code, so leaving out the population lets a viewer assume professional developers.
findings.suggestion: Say 'In a second experiment, mostly with computer-science students, ...'. That needs the participant passage in the corpus (generation.needsEvidence).

findings.explanation: The passage shows two re-checks, not 'several'. In one of them (the interaction model) the effect weakened and was no longer significant (p = 0.05). 'Kept its direction every time' is literally true, but it suggests a confirmation the passage does not give.
findings.suggestion: Say 'The authors re-checked it two other ways: the drop kept its direction both times, though in one it was too weak to be sure of.'

findings.explanation: 'Whether that turns into harder maintenance later is something none of this evidence tested' can be heard as saying no study tested later maintenance at all. That contradicts s24, where the Echoes trial did test it with other developers. What is untested is whether the same people's weaker understanding makes their own later changes harder, which is the scope the writer's note gives.
findings.suggestion: Say '... and whether that makes it harder for those same people to change their code later is something none of these studies tested.'

findings.explanation: "That study's participants" comes straight after the crowd-worker trial (s32-s33), whose people were mostly freelance or professional developers, so a viewer can hear this as the same people. The package says this experiment's 69 participants were mostly students, and the takeaway (s28) applies the result to reviewing a colleague's code.
findings.suggestion: Make the reference unambiguous and keep the population neutral: "In a separate experiment with different participants, working with AI cut their chance of answering questions about their own code correctly by 5.95 percentage points." Naming "mostly students" needs a passage the writer cannot record, so an editor may accept the neutral wording.
